text.en: What happens to people who must leave their homeland?

Aaraam Thinai is a supplementary prose piece by A. Muthulingam. It describes the pain of people who are uprooted from their native land, like plants pulled out of the soil, and who must face hardships as refugees or migrants. It records this wound that never heals.
The title means the sixth landscape: the Sangam tradition has five landscapes (ஐந்திணை), and the writer suggests that the world of the displaced is a sixth, painful one. The lesson makes us feel sympathy for refugees and for Tamil people who live abroad.
Terms to know: திணை (landscape category), புலம்பெயர்தல் (migration), தாய்மண் (motherland) and அவலம் (suffering). A supplementary lesson is for reading and understanding rather than for memorising.
